concerns.text: T004-IMPL (Training data) and T004b (Eval data) are both marked [P] (parallel-safe) but the description explicitly states T004b 'Must run AFTER T004-IMPL to ensure sequential writes to data_loader.py'. This is a hidden ordering dependency. If T004b runs in parallel, it will race with T004-IMPL on the shared `data_loader.py` file and potentially the `data/manifest.json` artifact, violating the 'Producer before consumer' and 'parallel-safe' rules.

T012-IMPL (loss_functions.py) is marked [P] but the description states it is 'NOT parallel-safe relative to T013 (train.py) as it is a strict prerequisite'. T013 depends on the code produced by T012. Marking T012 as [P] implies it can run concurrently with T013, which is impossible if T013 imports the module being written by T012. The [P] tag must be removed from T012-IMPL.

Tasks T028-T033 (Phase 7) are marked [P] and described as runnable in parallel 'once US1 and US2 are complete'. However, T029 (Confidence-Consistency Penalty) modifies `loss_functions.py` (produced in T012-IMPL/US1), and T030/T032/T033 depend on metrics generated by T018/T019 (US2). While they can start after US1/US2, they are not independent of each other if they all write to the same `code/analysis/stats.py` or `code/evaluation/run_benchmarks.py` files. Specifically, T030, T032, and T033 all target `code/analysis/stats.py`. Parallel execution of these tasks will cause file-write conflicts unless they are split into distinct files or the [P] tag is removed.

T004b is labeled 'BLOCKED' and 'Must run AFTER T004-IMPL', yet it is marked [P]. The [P] tag contradicts the explicit blocking dependency described in the text. The tag should be removed to reflect the sequential requirement.
